title: Application Security Defence
summary: Validate tokens and sessions, stop CSRF and replay, review code for bug classes and model threats with structured checks.
description: Application security is mostly careful checking: is this token really ours, is this session still allowed, did this request come from our own page, is this value safe to put in a query. You will validate a JWT-like token with a toy MAC, apply claim and clock rules, manage session lifetimes, enforce CSRF and replay defences, audit cookies and security headers, issue single-use reset tokens, validate redirect targets, enforce role and ownership checks, build a gatekeeper that combines them, then switch to secure code review (a banned-call scanner, safe query binding, taint tracing) and finish with structured threat modelling: trust-boundary checks and attack-tree costing. All tokens use a deliberately toy MAC (never use it for real) and every system, address and name is fictional.
outcomes: Validate tokens, sessions and requests, review code for bug classes and reason about threats with structured checks.
